messages:
Devon: Hey team - my rheum just recommended a specialty biologic (injectable) that requires prior auth and the pharmacy says they only ship via a specialty pharmacy network. I got two messages: one saying "PA required" and another 'SPP enrollment needed.' Can People Ops help with the PA docs and getting me enrolled in the specialty pharmacy program?

Harper (People Ops): Sorry you're in the queue, Devon. Yes we can help. Short checklist: 1) Prior auth packet from Dr. Chen (diagnosis, prior meds tried, labs) 2) Completed patient SPP consent/authorization (often required by specialty pharmacy) 3) Insurance EOB showing any prior trial or step therapy denials (if applicable) 4) Pharmacy contact info and the SPP enrollment form from them.

Devon: The specialty pharmacy portal asked for my carrier's plan code and group number. My digital ID shows a long member number only. Where do I find plan/group details?

Harper (People Ops): Use the carrier ID card FAQ page: https://benefits.redwood.com/ids . The plan/group is usually printed as "Plan: Redwood Medical PPO" and "Group: 1234567" on the PDF ID. If your digital card doesn't show it, upload a screenshot of the card and we can pull the plan/group for you.

Dr. Chen (Rheum): I can prepare a focused PA letter today. Include the following in the request: DX code (M05.9), history of failed DMARDs (list methotrexate, leflunomide), recent CRP/ESR labs (date + values), proposed biologic name/dose, and treatment rationale. I'll also attach a short medical necessity note addressing why this agent is preferred.

Devon: The specialty pharmacy (CareMax Specialty) emailed a form that asks me to sign an authorization to speak to the carrier and the provider. Is that the same as the HIPAA release? Anything People Ops needs me to sign?

Harper (People Ops): The pharmacy's SPP authorization is separate (it allows them to coordinate benefits and ship). We'll need either the pharmacy form or a signed pharmacy-specific consent plus a HIPAA release if you want us to act on your behalf with the carrier/clinic. We can email you both forms as a secure link.

PharmacyOpsBot: Enrollment link & docs: https://benefits.redwood.com/spp/enroll. Upload portal (secure): https://benefits.redwood.com/secure-upload (choose "Specialty Rx / PA"). Pharmacy contact: CareMax Specialty - enroll@caremaxsp.com / 1-800-555-2200.

Devon: Timeline? I need the first dose scheduled for next week if authorization clears.

Harper (People Ops): Typical carrier PA turnaround for specialty injectables is 3-7 business days with a completed packet. Specialty pharmacies can hold a starter supply pending approval in many cases; ask CareMax about a "starter dose" while PA is processed. If you upload the PA packet and the SPP consent today and mark subject "EXPEDITE - starter supply needed", we'll flag it as urgent and follow up directly with the carrier and CareMax.

Dr. Chen (Rheum): I'll send the PA letter + labs to Harper and copy Devon. I'll also note the patient needs a starter dose and why delay risks symptom flare.

Devon: Uploading CareMax form + screenshot of my digital ID now. Please send me the HIPAA release link so I can sign. Really appreciate the fast turnaround. :pray:

Harper (People Ops): Got it — will email the HIPAA + pharmacy consent secure links and watch for your upload. We'll confirm once we submit the PA and then post updates here. :thumbsup:
